title: Cabin Housekeeping: Keep Floor Mats/Bottles Clear of Pedals & Loose Projectiles Secured

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Top panels show one distant vehicle ahead on the road, not two vehicles facing each other in the same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: Cabin and pedal footwells are shown but no steering wheel is visible in any quadrant to indicate right-hand drive.

single_bulb_signal.note: No traffic signals are present in any quadrant.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Road seen through front windshield shows vehicle ahead in proper lane with centerline to left; no left-hand traffic violation visible.

zero_text.note: No letters, numbers, or words on bottles, bags, road, or plates; only red X icon top-left and green check icon top-right as graphic symbols.

scene_match.note: Shows bad vs good: bottom-left bottle jammed under brake pedal and top-left loose bags on shelf vs bottom-right clear pedals and top-right bags secured in cargo net, as prompted.

result.summary: Four-quadrant cabin housekeeping comparison clearly contrasts loose bottle under pedal and unsecured bags with clear pedals and net-secured cargo, with no text or traffic violations.

teaching_correct.note: Correctly teaches pedal obstruction and projectile hazard on left/red and secure stowage and clear footwell on right/green.

result.what_i_see: A four-panel illustration: top-left loose duffel bags on rear shelf with red X, top-right same bags secured in a cargo net with green check, bottom-left a plastic water bottle wedged under a brake pedal by a boot, bottom-right a clear footwell with pedals unobstructed.
